verified_boundaries: Registration cannot use a ceremony belonging to another authenticated user; concurrent challenge consumption has one winner.
Actual py_webauthn accepts UV=true synthetic cryptographic credentials and rejects UV=false for registration/authentication.
MFA rejection persists its attempt count; challenge, recovery/TOTP consumption, session and refresh creation roll back together on issuance failure.
TOTP persists the matched skew-window counter; used or older counter rejected; new/pending setup remains available and cannot downgrade concurrent confirmation.
Password reset generation is checked under user-row lock; concurrent code has one committed winner; cleanup failure cannot reauthorize code or delete newer request.
MFA/passkey responses expose optional canonical tenant_id, matching current principal/session identity.
limitations: No real browser/authenticator, SMTP delivery, Redis server, production account or production database validation. Redis and issuance-failure injection are deterministic fakes; PostgreSQL and cryptographic WebAuthn/TOTP verification are actual.
Legacy pending reset records lacking password_generation must request a fresh code; no migration or new table.
Existing authenticators that cannot perform user verification are rejected in line with existing required-UV options; no blanket hardware compatibility claim.
Pre-change TOTP timestamps remain conservative high-water marks until next accepted step; existing clock-skew window unchanged.
Existing passkey clone-cleanup wording/rollback behavior predates this slice and is not certified as durable disablement.
Commit cannot guarantee response delivery. A lost successful response requires normal new login/challenge rather than reusing a consumed factor.
